ATS

Job portals pass your CV through an applicant tracking system (ATS) that pulls the text out of the PDF. Here you set what the PDF says about itself, check what the machine finds, and see the order in which it reads your CV.

PDF properties

Saved with this CV version. Leave a field empty and it follows your CV automatically.

Upload a Text PDF to job portals (Download PDF → Print / Save as Text PDF); the one-column version is the safest. Browsers only let a Text PDF carry the title and the language, and most of them suggest the title as its file name. The Image PDF carries every property, but its text is a picture an ATS cannot read. Keywords are rarely used by an ATS: the words in your CV are what count.

Checks

What a parser looks for first.

    Match a job ad

    Paste the job ad, or at least its tasks and requirements. Blatt picks out its key terms and shows which ones your CV already uses: an ATS ranks applicants by these words, and recruiters search for them. Nothing leaves your browser, and the ad is saved with this CV version.

    Word / Google Docs

    Write your CV in the supplied Word template, then import the completed document. Google Docs is supported by downloading the document as a Microsoft Word (.docx) file first.

    Keep the template’s title, subtitle, heading levels, labels, and bullet structure. Tables, text boxes, and custom layouts are not imported.
